evidence.curator_note: EXPERIMENTAL CONTEXT: this is the dissociation of the mass-selected even-electron oxonium ion C2H5O+=CHCH3 (m/z 73), itself generated by EI alpha-cleavage of diethyl ether; not a 70 eV EI reaction of a molecular ion. The 'rH' label is a reaction-type mark (i = inductive, rH = H-rearrangement), NOT an electron-pushing arrow (0 arcs drawn). No abundance is printed for this channel; product left detected=false, peak status inferred. (Text: this m/z 45 HO+=CHCH3 is NOT isomeric C2H5O+.) Eq 8.13, lower ('rH') branch of the fork from C2H5O(+)=CHCH3 (m/z 73). Hydrogen rearrangement cleaving two bonds (text: cf. Eqs 4.43, 8.11; the higher PA of acetaldehyde makes 8.13 favoured over 8.11): a beta-hydrogen (H6, on the terminal methyl C1) transfers to oxygen O3 while the C1-C2 double bond forms and the C2-O3 bond breaks, expelling neutral ethylene C2H4 (IE/PA 7.0 eV printed) and giving protonated acetaldehyde HO(+)=CHCH3 (m/z 45; text notes this m/z 45 ion is NOT the isomeric C2H5O+, confirmed by the C2H5OC2D5 labelling giving m/z 46 and 49). Encoded as a concerted 4-membered TS (O3-C2-C1-H6): move <1> C1-H6 bonding pair -> C1=C2 pi bond; move <2> C2-O3 bonding pair -> new O3-H6 sigma bond. Book draws 0 electron-pushing arcs; the page shows only the net reaction arrow labelled 'rH' and product formulae, so BOTH 2-electron moves are implied by the reaction type, not drawn. No percentage is printed for this channel on the page.

Cross-link: MØD rule IMS_8_13 ('Field Rule 8.13 rH', src/data_generation/rules/IMS_chap8_examples.py). PARTIAL MATCH / neutral-loss mis-encoding. Its LHS matches this substrate exactly (rule H4 on C1 -> O8, C5-O8 cleavage: same atoms as my H6 on C1 -> O3, C2-O3 cleavage) and its ionic product [H]4[O+]8{=}[C]9(H1)[C]11(H3) reproduces HO(+)=CHCH3 (m/z 45) correctly. HOWEVER the rule writes the ethylene neutral as [C]1(H2)[C]5(H2) with a SINGLE C1-C5 bond (a .CH2-CH2. 1,2-diradical), OMITTING the C1=C5 double bond that this record forms; mass (28) is unaffected but the neutral's bond order is under-specified. See rule_mismatches.
